opening_message:

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee whose role owns the Payroll system, write is within policy; recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Requested write exceeds max; recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR reports full-time Payroll Specialist (max write), while Security reports contractor with basic security training (max read for contractors without advanced training). Given the conflicting records, I apply the more restrictive policy. As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed is read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant read.

2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

The Security agent says contractor with basic training → max is read.
